gaps.remediation: Keep the published incident response plan and supported versions policy current. Record a product response exercise and evidence of advisory and notification procedures. Your organization approves, exercises, and records its own deployment response.
gaps.title: Incident response and advisory operation still need evidence

gaps.remediation: Write decision records through one record writer into a hash-chained local audit with signed heads, then add a command that exports them for assessors.
gaps.title: Gate decision records are not tamper-evident and cannot be exported

gaps.remediation: Authenticate every inbound request to the relay and allow only listed senders and channels, as planned for the relay.
gaps.title: The messaging relay has no inbound authentication yet

gaps.remediation: Attest the release artifacts with GitHub artifact attestations in the Release workflow, and verify them when the dashboard data is refreshed.
gaps.title: No build provenance or attestation for the VSIX, the relay image or the package

gaps.remediation: Build an SBOM of the relay image and scan it with a pinned, checksummed scanner, reporting high and critical findings.
gaps.title: No vulnerability scan or SBOM for the relay container image

gaps.remediation: Run static analysis on every pull request and on main, and keep its results as evidence.
gaps.title: No static analysis of the source code

gaps.remediation: Add a CODEOWNERS file that names the owner for the gate paths and the compliance sources.
gaps.title: No CODEOWNERS file; review routing is by convention

gaps.remediation: The hub's backup, restore and restore drill are documented; the relay's operator runbook adds its backups, restore and upgrades.
gaps.title: No backup and recovery guidance for the messaging relay

gaps.remediation: Publish one threat model and a data-flow diagram per component, each reviewed at least once a year.
gaps.title: No standalone threat model or data-flow diagram

gaps.remediation: Keep exact versions for root dependencies, turn install scripts off where the build allows it, and turn on alerts for security updates only.
gaps.title: Root install scripts and automated security update alerts still need closure

gaps.remediation: Extension, relay and hub maintainers publish the event inventory, map tested event generation and provide a supported forwarding option for required logs. The deployment operator approves the required event list and verifies representative events arrive at the configured log destination, are retained for the approved period, and can be retrieved for review.
gaps.title: Deployment audit event coverage, forwarding and retention need evidence

gaps.remediation: Make the docs check (and later the compliance check) required on main; the owner changes this repository setting, and the gap closes when the settings collector sees it.
gaps.title: The docs build is not a required check

gaps.remediation: Check the platform's TCB status, certificate revocation and the enclave's measurements against the provider's published build; until then the security policy says so and points to the provider's full verifier.
gaps.title: The attestation checks do not check TCB status, certificate revocation or enclave measurements

gaps.remediation: Staff maintainers verify invitation approval, signed role changes and removal through the production staff and hub flow. The deployment identity owner approves eligible accounts and roles, samples an account review and offboarding, and records the approved roster and revocation results.
gaps.title: Staff account lifecycle needs release and deployment evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment sponsor and endpoint operator identify the approved malware protection provider for each in-scope workstation and hosted component. Obtain the policy and current coverage record, then record the result of an approved benign detection exercise. If a component lacks coverage, assign its deployment owner to implement the missing protection and retest.
gaps.title: Deployment malware protection needs implementation or inheritance evidence

gaps.remediation: Extension policy and label maintainers verify signed attribute changes, including absent, revoked or wrong-purpose authority. The deployment information owner lists each in-scope output and its marking rule. Collect the signed test configuration, allow and refusal records, and labelled output samples. Implement and retest missing markings or document an approved scope exclusion.
gaps.title: Release evidence for authorized label changes and output markings

gaps.remediation: Staff and gate maintainers demonstrate that role restrictions apply during approval, routine work and privileged actions, including a denial when a person holds incompatible roles. The deployment identity and security owners approve the role matrix and sample privilege reviews, separate privileged accounts, and the allowed and denied action audit records.
gaps.title: Operational separation of duties and privileges need evidence

gaps.remediation: Component maintainers and the deployment monitoring operator exercise audit write and capacity failures on each in-scope component. Verify operator notification delivery, timing and response. Record approved timestamp granularity and synchronization, then compare representative records from the assessed components. Track missing alerts or clock controls for implementation and retest.
gaps.title: Deployment audit failure alerts and clock settings need evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment identity owner and component maintainers inventory the authenticators in scope. Record approved issuance and recovery, strength and storage requirements, rotation and revocation. Exercise revocation and stale cached credential denial where applicable. Identify missing controls and retest them before closure.
gaps.title: Deployment authenticator lifecycle needs verified evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment sponsor designates the identity policy owner and approves the policy and procedures for the assessed systems. The identity policy owner specifies responsible roles and review intervals, documents dissemination and review, and provides the signed policy and versioned approval, distribution and review records.
gaps.title: Deployment identification and authentication policy needs approval and evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment identity owner approves how individual, group, role, service and device identifiers are authorized, assigned and protected from reuse, and defines which user statuses must be recorded. Component maintainers trace these rules through the relevant staff or device workflows in the assessed release. Collect the identifier policy, status rules and redacted assignment, change and offboarding records. Document inheritance or missing controls for each applicable component.
gaps.title: Identifier assignment and user status need deployment evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment sponsor establishes the required identity assurance levels and names the registration authority and privacy owner. The registration authority records how it resolves a unique individual, receives identity evidence, validates and verifies it, performs the applicable in-person check and sends out-of-band confirmation to the recorded address. Collect approved procedures and redacted attestations or authorized evidence references. Document sponsor-approved applicability decisions and keep identity documents in the authorized storage location.
gaps.title: Deployment identity proofing needs sponsor and registration authority evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment identity and network owners approve which device classes and connection boundaries require authentication before access. Component maintainers and the deployment operators document the device identity, enrollment, trust settings and revocation at each boundary. Collect redacted results showing an enrolled device is admitted and an unknown or revoked device is refused before the connection is established. Record inherited controls and assign fixes for applicable boundaries without a verified mechanism.
gaps.title: Device authentication needs connection-specific evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment identity owner inventories each interactive sign-in and recovery surface and identifies the operator responsible for it. For each password-based surface, collect provider or component evidence for the password blocklist, protected transport, approved salted storage where passwords are stored, recovery reset and approved password selection rules. For every in-scope authentication surface, verify that input and responses obscure sensitive authentication details. Retain redacted screenshots and permitted and denied test results. Review password-specific applicability separately from feedback protection.
gaps.title: Interactive authentication needs password and feedback evidence

gaps.remediation: Release maintainers associate the existing source scan with the exact candidate commit and record its scope and exceptions. Review unpacked installers and other shipped artifacts, then have the deployment operator review applicable images, scripts, configuration and static stores for embedded unencrypted authenticators. Record the artifact digests, coverage, redacted results and reviewed exception dispositions. Remediate confirmed findings and rescan. Identify how skipped formats and files are assessed.
gaps.title: Release and deployment artifacts need embedded authenticator review

gaps.remediation: The deployment security owner confirms which cryptographic modules are in scope and which module authentication requirements apply. The module operator and component maintainers document the deployed module identity, version and mode, its boundary, operator roles and authentication mechanisms. Collect configuration and redacted authorized and denied operation results. Where a validation is required, verify its applicability to the configured module, version and operating mode. Record and remediate unsupported requirements before closure.
gaps.title: Cryptographic module authentication needs deployment evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment sponsor approves the in-scope sign-in paths, account classes, accounts and services assigned to single sign-on, replay resistance selections and reauthentication triggers. Identity and component operators trace unique user identities to processes acting for them. Collect redacted policy exports and results showing strong multi-factor authentication for privileged accounts, multi-factor authentication for non-privileged accounts, replay refusal, single sign-on to assigned services and a fresh challenge at each applicable trigger. Use G3 relay ingress and Phase 76 requester binding only for that part of the deployment. Assign implementation or inheritance verification where a path lacks evidence.
gaps.title: Organizational sign-in needs deployment authentication evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment identity risk owner identifies where the same individuals hold accounts on multiple assessed systems and obtains sponsor approval of measures to limit cross-system compromise. Collect a redacted account and service inventory, approved authenticator reuse controls and operating evidence for the selected mechanism. Sample that independent credentials, centrally managed sign-in or another approved mechanism operates as designed. Record inherited coverage and route unmitigated reuse to its operator.
gaps.title: Authenticator reuse across systems needs a deployment risk review

gaps.remediation: The deployment sponsor records whether external users or processes and federated credentials are in scope and approves participating organizations, external authenticators, required assurance levels and profiles. Verify that each in-scope external user is uniquely authenticated and bound to any process acting for them. Where required, demonstrate electronic verification of public key credentials from approved Government of Canada departments and agencies. Collect a redacted issuer and authenticator inventory, conformance evidence, accepted and denied sign-in receipts for approved and unapproved credentials, and the sponsor decision for each excluded path.
gaps.title: External authentication and federation need sponsor-approved scope

gaps.remediation: The deployment sponsor determines where public key infrastructure is used for authentication. The deployment public key infrastructure owner approves a common method to provision, update and remove trust anchors across in-scope network, operating system, browser and application platforms. Collect the redacted trust-store inventory and sampled configuration and change records. Verify that an authorized trust anchor works and that an unapproved or removed anchor is refused. Record gaps and sponsor-approved applicability decisions per platform.
gaps.title: Public key trust stores need deployment governance evidence

gaps.remediation: The sponsor continuity lead approves the policy and deployment contingency plan and records who receives and reviews them. Retain the critical asset and dependency inventory, named escalation roles, coordination records for related plans, degraded processing/telecommunications/environment capacity analysis, and approved resumption objectives for essential functions.
gaps.title: Approved contingency policy, critical assets and recovery priorities need evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment continuity exercise lead identifies the required trainees and role-specific training schedule, reviews training when roles or systems change, and coordinates a test with the owners of related plans. Record the dated training and exercise results, approved scenarios, corrective actions and retests. Use the hub restore drill as a component input when the hub is in scope.
gaps.title: Contingency role training and coordinated exercises need dated records

gaps.remediation: The deployment hosting and continuity owners identify the alternate sites required by the approved recovery plan. For storage, verify retrieval agreements, equivalent controls, separation from common threats and mitigations for regional access loss. For processing, verify resumption agreements and priority provisions, equipment and approved settings, access and shared-risk analysis, tested readiness and a plan for permanent loss of the primary site. Obtain an authorized applicability decision for any exclusions.
gaps.title: Alternate storage and processing sites need approved scope and readiness evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment network and service-contract owners document primary and alternate paths for in-scope processing and storage sites. Verify recovery time and service-priority provisions, provider and physical route independence, and shared points of failure. Record priority access requests when the approved scope requires them, perform scheduled failover tests, and retain the dated results and remediation.
gaps.title: Alternate telecommunications agreements and exercises need evidence

gaps.remediation: Backup operators and component maintainers inventory backups, owners and critical assets. Verify scheduled integrity and retrieval tests, separate storage and protected transfer within approved recovery targets, dual authorization for protected backup deletion, and cryptographic protection and key access. Link component restore and relay runbook evidence where applicable and assign deficiencies for implementation and retest.
gaps.title: Backup reliability, transfer, removal authority and cryptographic protections need evidence

gaps.remediation: Deployment recovery operators and component maintainers identify transaction-based stores, critical components and protected recovery tools. Exercise rollback or journal recovery on each applicable transaction store and restore components from approved integrity-checked baselines. Measure time to known operational state, verify protection and access limits on recovery components, and record sponsor decisions for inapplicable objectives.
gaps.title: Transaction and component recovery need scoped drills and protected inputs

gaps.remediation: The deployment identity owner approves the failed-attempt threshold, time window and automatic response for each applicable sign-in path. The sign-in operator records the active settings. Using authorized test accounts, verify the response when the limit is exceeded and collect redacted results for the required lock, delay, notification or recovery behavior. Record inherited mechanisms and assign gaps to the responsible component or provider.
gaps.title: Failed sign-in limits and responses need deployment evidence

gaps.remediation: The sponsor approves the notice text with privacy and security owners and documents each action allowed before authentication with its rationale in the system security plan. Interface and service operators inventory public and restricted entry points. Collect redacted captures of notice timing and required acknowledgment before access, and test that approved public actions work while protected actions require authentication. Record any distinct notice for publicly accessible systems.
gaps.title: System use notices and actions before authentication need review

gaps.remediation: The deployment endpoint owner records which workstations and managed devices are in scope. The sponsor approves inactivity thresholds and unattended locking rules. Collect managed settings and redacted captures showing the inactivity or manual lock as applicable, previously visible information concealed by a publicly viewable lock display, and access restored only through approved authentication. Assign missing inherited or component controls for implementation and retest.
gaps.title: Device locking and obscured displays need endpoint evidence

gaps.remediation: Deployment identity and session operators identify in-scope local, browser and remote user sessions. The sponsor approves when users must log out and the conditions for automatic session termination. Collect the approved user procedure and deployed settings. Exercise the configured triggers and verify that the old session cannot continue or regain protected access. Record any approved work allowed to continue after termination and its access boundary.
gaps.title: Inactivity logout and logical session termination need evidence

gaps.remediation: The sponsor authorizes each applicable remote access method and documents its conditions and privileged-use rationale in the system security plan. Network and service operators record managed entry points, monitoring and control settings, session cryptographic configuration and approved dedicated management consoles. Collect redacted tests for allowed access, denied unapproved paths and denied privileged access from ordinary endpoints, plus trustworthy records of authorized remote privileged commands and access to security-relevant information.
gaps.title: Remote access methods and privileged access need deployment evidence

gaps.remediation: The sponsor identifies which external systems may access the deployment or process, store or transmit its information. Deployment operators verify those systems against approved security and privacy controls and retain applicable connection or processing agreements. Record authorized restrictions for portable storage and prohibited network-accessible storage. Collect the approved system inventory, verification records and representative permitted and refused access and storage tests, with evidence references for sensitive agreements.
gaps.title: External system use and storage restrictions need deployment evidence

gaps.remediation: The sponsor and information owner identify applicable sharing with external public-sector organizations and sharing between or within federal institutions. Retain authorized references to the applicable written agreements or arrangements and their safeguarding terms. Component and deployment operators demonstrate how users compare partner authorization to the information restrictions and collect redacted results for allowed and disallowed sharing. Reuse approved export-control evidence only for that part of the assessed boundary.
gaps.title: Information-sharing safeguards and agreements need deployment evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment audit policy owner approves the scope, roles, responsibilities and audit procedures with the component and monitoring owners. Record who received the policy, its accountable official and review triggers, and confirm the procedures reflect the deployment boundary and applicable obligations.
gaps.title: Deployment audit and accountability policy needs approval and operating records

gaps.remediation: Extension, relay and hub maintainers map the approved AU-02 event inventory to generation tests for every assessed component. Capture redacted records proving event type, time, component or location, source, outcome and relevant actor or entity, plus each approved additional field. The deployment audit owner approves the list and verifies who can select the events. Document adjustments and retest omissions without exposing secrets or record payloads.
gaps.title: Selected component events and audit record fields need coverage evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment logging operator and component owners document expected and peak volumes, retention, local buffer limits and capacity for all assessed sources. Verify scheduled offloading of audit records to the designated separate store and reconcile a measured sample from production and retrieval. Exercise delivery loss and recovery, track any unforwarded records, and retest gaps. Use Phase 84 for the relay runbook when the relay is in scope.
gaps.title: Audit capacity planning and offloading need measured deployment evidence

gaps.remediation: Deployment monitoring and incident response owners approve review cadence, review triggers, reporting recipients, and the sources and clock tolerance for a system-wide trail. Component maintainers provide redacted event samples. Demonstrate central review, correlation across repositories and automated routing of a harmless test event to the approved response process. Record measured clock tolerance, owner review and follow-up, then assign and retest coverage gaps.
gaps.title: Audit review, centralized analysis and time correlation need operating evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment audit analyst and reporting system owner identify approved search and sorting fields and the reporting tool. Generate an on-demand review and a representative incident report from sanitized source records. Compare source checksums and record order before and after reduction to verify that the tool preserves original records. Assign missing capabilities to the component or monitoring owner and retest.
gaps.title: Audit analysis and reports need authorized field searches and source integrity evidence

gaps.remediation: Deployment logging and identity owners review the audit store topology and approved separation frequency. Verify the store is on a physically different system or component where required. Review the privileged roles authorized to administer logging, and the separate read-only roles. Test allowed reads, denied changes and deletions, and delivery of unauthorized-change alerts through an approved exercise. Component maintainers preserve scoped file permission evidence and investigate missing protection.
gaps.title: Audit infrastructure separation, privileged roles and protection alerts need evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment configuration manager obtains sponsor approval for the policy and management plan. Record accountable roles, approved items under configuration control, management and change procedures, protections for the plan, and distribution and review records. Collect a sampled application of the approved workflow.
gaps.title: Configuration policy and management plan need deployment approval

gaps.remediation: Release maintainers and deployment configuration operators identify assessed hardware, firmware and software versions and settings. Separate production from development and test, record review triggers and retained prior versions, and demonstrate automated reconciliation, detected drift and rollback to a known configuration. Use exact-release installer inventory as an input and retain environment-specific settings separately.
gaps.title: Configuration baselines need automated reconciliation, retained versions and separated environments

gaps.remediation: The sponsor and endpoint security owner identify approved high-risk travel conditions and devices. Verify provisioning from the restricted baseline, authorized assignment and required measures on return. Retain an approved baseline and redacted provisioning and return sample, or the authorized scope decision.
gaps.title: High-risk travel device configuration and return evidence need approved scope

gaps.remediation: Release maintainers and deployment change authority sample a configuration-controlled change. Record security and privacy impact review with named representatives, approval or refusal, effective access restrictions, isolated test validation, monitored change deployment and post-change verification of each affected control. Include review records and applicable authorized-access decisions. Use G7 and G12 only for their scoped repository evidence.
gaps.title: Deployment change decisions, impacts and authorized access need a verified change trace

gaps.remediation: Component maintainers and deployment security operators approve the applicable restrictive baseline and essential functions, ports, protocols, services and software. Compare applied settings to the approved baseline, record authorized exceptions and monitoring, review unused functions, and test permitted and denied program execution under the approved allow-by-exception policy. Record gaps in deployed host or application enforcement and retest.
gaps.title: Secure settings, least-functionality review and approved execution need evidence

gaps.remediation: Deployment asset and component owners reconcile scoped assets, responsible administrators, assessed configurations and approved deviations with installation, removal and update records. Demonstrate approved automated detection using a synthetic unauthorized component and record the configured response. Use release inventories as evidence for supplier artifacts and verify actual deployments independently.
gaps.title: Installed components need accountable inventory and automated unauthorized component response

gaps.remediation: Deployment software asset and endpoint administration owners approve installation and peer-to-peer use rules. Record applicable licence entitlements and reconcile constrained quantities. Demonstrate allowed privileged installation, denied ordinary-user installation and monitoring. Collect software exception and peer-to-peer restrictions where applicable and track implementation gaps.
gaps.title: Software use, licences and privileged user installations need operating evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment data steward and component maintainers inventory approved information types, processing and storage locations, and users with access. Include approved provider, relay, hub and local scope as applicable. Sample authorized location changes and test the approved automated discovery tool against seeded benign data in each assessed component. Record scope or sensing gaps for follow-up and preserve only sanitized references.
gaps.title: Information locations, access and automated discovery need scoped deployment evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment sponsor designates the access control policy owner and approves the policy and operating procedures for the assessed system. The policy owner records scope, responsibilities, coordination and distribution, and sets review intervals and triggers. Retain the signed version, named owner, dissemination record and schedule and samples for policy and procedure review.
gaps.title: Deployment access control policy needs approval and evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment identity owner approves managed account types, automated lifecycle mechanisms, expiry and inactivity limits, high-risk criteria and disablement deadlines. Using authorized test identities, verify temporary and emergency expiry, disablement for expiration, inactivity, separation, policy violation and significant risk, and automatic auditing of creation, modification, enabling, disabling and removal. Retain redacted event and timing evidence. The catalogue incorporates shared-account credential changes into AC-02. Reconcile the selected AC-02(10) row with the sponsor, recording AC-02 evidence for any shared accounts and an approved tailoring decision.
gaps.title: Account automation, disablement and audit need deployment evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment identity owner approves the role-based or attribute-based scheme and the authorities who assign privileged accounts. Account operators inventory applicable privileged assignments and monitor changes. Collect redacted configuration, sampled approved assignments, change-monitoring records and timely revocation evidence. Verify that a removed assignment cannot use the privileged action.
gaps.title: Privileged account assignment and removal need monitoring evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment sponsor and privilege owners identify actions with significant impact that require separate authorized approvers. Implement or verify enforcement for those actions and retain the approved action and approver mapping. Exercise denial with one approver, denial when the same identity attempts both approvals, and success with two eligible approvers. Where relevant, use the product gate's per-action decision evidence as input and verify the second independent approval at the assessed enforcement boundary.
gaps.title: Dual authorization for designated actions needs evidence

gaps.remediation: The sponsor and access policy owner identify the subjects, objects and discretionary access policy in scope. Component and deployment operators verify how authorized holders may share information, delegate privileges, set or change attributes, or change access rules, where the policy permits those actions. Collect the reviewed policy and exact-release allowed and refused results. Include the staff roster and cell access rules only for the component and operations those rules govern.
gaps.title: Discretionary access decisions need scoped permission evidence

gaps.remediation: The sponsor and information release owner define what may leave the system, which receiving systems are eligible and which safeguards and validation they require. Operators and component maintainers verify configured release routes and content validation for each applicable channel. Retain approved policies, receiver safeguard evidence and redacted records of releases allowed and refused for content or destination. Use model-route and export eligibility evidence only for the routes it covers.
gaps.title: Controlled information release needs destination and approval evidence

gaps.remediation: The sponsor authorizes each permitted wireless access type and appoints the wireless network and endpoint administrators. Collect the approved inventory and configuration requirements, effective encryption and required user or device authentication settings, pre-issuance evidence for disabled unused radios and the authorized wireless configurator roles. Exercise admission and refusal for the approved boundary and verify that unauthorized roles cannot change wireless settings.
gaps.title: Wireless access and configuration restrictions need deployment evidence

gaps.remediation: The sponsor and endpoint management owner identify and authorize organization-controlled mobile devices, including use outside controlled areas, and approve the required full-device or container encryption. Collect the approved fleet and enrollment scope, effective device management and encryption settings, and redacted tests showing that conforming devices can connect and unapproved or nonconforming devices are refused. Record inheritances and reviewed exclusions. Where collectors are deployed, use their enrollment records only for their device binding.
gaps.title: Managed mobile access and encryption need deployment evidence

gaps.remediation: The sponsor designates authorized public publishers and names the privacy or security reviewer and the operator who can remove content. Document the assessed public channels and capture publisher authorization and training, a prepublication review record, the recurring review schedule and completed sample, and an approved removal exercise or a real redacted removal record. Identify the review and release process for each public channel in scope.
gaps.title: Public posting authority and content review need operating evidence

gaps.remediation: The sponsor system integrity lead approves the policy and procedures, identifies component and operations responsibilities, and records coordination, distribution and review. Verify a representative flaw, protection or monitoring work item followed the approved procedure.
gaps.title: System integrity policy and procedures need approved operating evidence

gaps.remediation: Release maintainers and deployment patch operators map scoped supported component and firmware versions to security updates. Validate applicable fixes in a representative test environment and prove an automated deployment inventory distinguishes applied, overdue and excepted updates. Keep release dependency observations and approved deployment exceptions with their dated remediation result.
gaps.title: Automated installed-update inventory and patch closure need deployment evidence

gaps.remediation: Deployment endpoint and hosted security owners identify each malware protection update mechanism and its privileged approving role. Verify a permitted update and denial for an ordinary role or unauthorized configuration change. Capture redacted policy and audit receipts from each assessed protection mechanism and track uncovered assets through G15.
gaps.title: Malware protection updates need privileged authorization and activity evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment monitoring and network owners approve monitored interfaces, ingress and egress anomaly criteria, alert recipients and collection boundary, including separately approved visibility for encrypted traffic. Use benign synthetic events to verify timely analysis, deployed event baselines and anomaly recognition, automated operator alerts and response. Where assessed, verify wireless protection and monitoring at the wired boundary. Record approved limits, configuration and observed results per mechanism.
gaps.title: Monitoring and alerts need verified coverage, privacy scope and operating evidence

gaps.remediation: Component maintainers and deployment integrity and incident response owners approve the software, firmware and information to verify, checking schedule and recipients. Demonstrate centrally managed settings and notifications by detecting a harmless changed test artifact, then record incident intake and corrective action. Use G4 attestations as supplier provenance and verify deployed monitoring and response separately.
gaps.title: Deployed integrity checks and violation response need tested coverage

gaps.remediation: The deployment messaging and endpoint owners identify applicable message ingress and egress and the protection mechanism supplied by each assessed provider. Verify approved automatic update cadence and detection and action for harmless simulated unsolicited messages on each applicable boundary. Obtain authorized scope treatment for unused messaging surfaces.
gaps.title: Message boundary spam protection and automatic updates need verified applicability

gaps.remediation: Component maintainers and deployment security owners inventory approved input surfaces and error audiences for the extension, relay and hub as assessed. Run benign invalid input, malformed message and out-of-scope data tests and verify safe refusal and permitted diagnostic detail. Capture redacted user and operator error samples and verify sensitive values remain absent. Assign and retest uncovered interfaces.
gaps.title: Component input validation and role-scoped errors need traceable tests

gaps.remediation: The deployment endpoint and privileged access owners identify assessed processes and the approved host memory-execution protections. Verify those settings on sampled assessed hosts. Separately inventory dedicated physical administration workstations and allowed task and network boundaries, show their isolation and verify privileged actions are restricted to the approved workstations. Record approved scope decisions and gaps.
gaps.title: Managed memory protections and dedicated administration workstations need deployment evidence

gaps.remediation: The sponsor risk authority approves risk assessment and response procedures, owners, review triggers and tolerance. Sample an actual finding through assignment, accepted treatment or remediation, authorized approval and follow-up. Record scope, residual risk, review or expiry date and reassessment responsibility.
gaps.title: Assessment policy and risk treatment decisions need authority and follow-up evidence

gaps.remediation: The sponsor categorization and risk owners approve information impact and handling decisions. Component maintainers supply current data flows and trust boundaries. Review the actual deployment threat and privacy risks, critical assets and supporting dependencies and verify traceability to selected safeguards and open actions.
gaps.title: System sensitivity, risks and critical dependencies need assessed deployment evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment procurement and risk owners identify assessed suppliers, services, release dependencies and trust boundaries. Release maintainers supply available inventory and provenance. Assess concentration, integrity and continuity risks, record owners and treatments, and retain the review trigger and date. Use supplier evidence and approved exception references rather than unverified assertions.
gaps.title: Supply chain risk assessments need reviewed service and dependency scope

gaps.remediation: The deployment vulnerability management owner approves scope, schedule, coverage, detection content updates and any authorized elevated scanner identities. Reconcile scoped assets against inventory and verify current detection content and authorized access in a permitted test environment. Review and track redacted results. Preserve exact release inventory checks and verify deployments separately.
gaps.title: Vulnerability monitoring needs current coverage and bounded scan authority

gaps.remediation: Product security and deployment intake owners verify the published instructions reach the approved private channel. Exercise a clearly marked benign report through receipt, triage and owner handoff, retaining restricted and redacted evidence. Record how deployed services receive reports or inherit the approved organizational route.
gaps.title: Public reporting instructions and private vulnerability intake need an exercised handoff

gaps.remediation: The sponsor security and privacy owners approve planning policy and procedures, named responsibilities and the assessed boundary. Complete the system security and privacy plan with current component and trust-boundary diagrams, data flows, roles, requirements, shared responsibilities, exceptions and links to assessor evidence. Record review and release or deployment change triggers.
gaps.title: System security and privacy plans need approved deployment scope and diagrams

gaps.remediation: Deployment access and privacy owners approve rules of behaviour and external application and public posting restrictions. Verify the rules reach assigned users, acknowledgements or equivalent authorized records exist before access and on revision, and applicable external access restrictions have an operating sample. Record approved scope for external services.
gaps.title: Rules of behaviour and external-site restrictions need acknowledged deployment records

gaps.remediation: The sponsor security and privacy authorities approve the applicable baseline and overlays using categorization and deployment boundaries. Link every inclusion, enhancement, inheritance, exclusion or alternative to its rationale, affected control and component, approving authority and evidence or open action. Reassess the baseline when the release, configuration or scope changes.
gaps.title: Selected control baselines and tailoring need authorized decisions

gaps.remediation: The deployment incident response lead assigns role-specific training and exercise cadence, then coordinates a representative drill with continuity, privacy and other applicable plan owners. Retain attendance, scope, scenario, measured performance, corrective actions and follow-up retest. Use supplier drills only for the exercised component and event.
gaps.title: Response training and coordinated exercises need dated deployment evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment response and continuity leads and component maintainers identify incident classes, required mission continuity actions and approved dynamic response mechanisms. Exercise a benign declared event through detection, analysis, containment, recovery and a continuity decision. Record the authorized roles, measured transitions, tool readiness and follow-up.
gaps.title: Incident handling and continuity actions need a tested response trace

gaps.remediation: The sponsor response lead, privacy authority and approved external partners agree the incident information categories, purpose, recipient, handling and coordination procedure. Demonstrate an authorized sanitized exchange and correlation in a drill. Keep an approved agreement or equivalent record, its scope and evidence reference.
gaps.title: External incident correlation and information sharing need authorized evidence

gaps.remediation: The deployment incident operations, vulnerability and supplier coordination owners define tracking fields, reporting times, approved recipients and mechanisms. Exercise a synthetic incident through tracking, authorized automated notification, related flaw disclosure and applicable supplier handoff. Retain delivery and acknowledgement timestamps, recorded disposition and evidence of restricted recipients.
gaps.title: Incident tracking and automated reporting need demonstrated handoffs

gaps.remediation: Partners whose systems are not like ours can send files whose label cannot be checked: a binding with no signature, a signature by an anchor your organization has not pinned for that partner, a form this version cannot check yet, a marking read from the file's text, or no label at all. Such files are held in quarantine in a protected cell at a provisional label, and an exchange officer confirms, raises or sets the label; a label lower than the sender's is refused. A person's confirmation is recorded as that person's act, never as a check of the file, so a mistaken confirmation is the risk that remains. Setting the label of an unlabelled arrival below its holding ceiling (the agreement's ceiling, released to no one) is not lowering: the holding label is your organization's protective default, not the sender's claim. Your organization's security officer accepts this condition; pinning each partner's signing anchors in exchangePartners turns claimed labels into checked ones. A label counts as checked only while the person who recorded the arrival is an exchange officer and the partner's anchor is still pinned, so removing an anchor turns that partner's earlier arrivals back into not checked.
